summary: The portfolio page outage originates in portfolio-service, not api-gateway. At 09:52 a config change (cfg-2207, infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small') cut portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5. Within ~1 minute Hikari reported total=5, active=5, idle=0 with 20-57 callers waiting and 3000ms JDBC acquire timeouts; db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 (was ~12). portfolio-service p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~4.2s, so api-gateway's /v1/portfolio/holdings calls timed out -> 504s and gateway p99 ~4.3s / 7% 5xx. Request rate (~560/s), CPU (~36%) and memory (~57%) were flat, ruling out load-driven saturation or resource exhaustion. The suspected gateway deploy dep-5220 (h2 upgrade) was at 08:00, ~1h45m before onset, and order-service (the other h2-switched upstream) is entirely unaffected. A comparable past incident (HIST-115) was the same class of pool misconfiguration. Primary fix: revert cfg-2207.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service DB connection pool shrunk to 5 by cost-optimisation config change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2207 set portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 09:52, drastically under-provisioning the Hikari connection pool. Under normal load (flat ~560 req/s), requests immediately queued for connections, hit the 3000ms acquire timeout, and portfolio-service slowed to ~4s; api-gateway then timed out on /v1/portfolio/holdings returning 504s, producing the reported gateway p99 spike. Fault originates in portfolio-service configuration (the gateway is only the symptom surface).

causal_chain.claim: Pool sized at 5; db_pool_in_use pins at 5.0 and Hikari reports total=5, idle=0 with long waiting queues
Requests can't acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms -> portfolio-service p99 jumps to ~4s at 09:48 bucket
api-gateway /v1/portfolio/holdings calls time out -> 504s and gateway p99 ~4.3s

assumptions: No other simultaneous change to portfolio-service datasource beyond cfg-2207
Normal request volume (~560 req/s) genuinely required the larger pool

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2-to-upstream upgrade (dep-5220) broke portfolio-service calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5220 (envoy 1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service/order-service) deployed at 08:00 introduced a gateway-side fault causing 4s latencies and 504s to portfolio-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Deploy at 08:00 is ~1h45m before onset (09:45); order-service, the other h2-switched upstream, is completely unaffected (F8); the errors are inside portfolio-service as JDBC/Hikari pool exhaustion (F4), not HTTP/2 protocol errors; gateway had no errors until the pool change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load growth / capacity saturation on portfolio-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A traffic surge outgrew portfolio-service capacity, saturating the connection pool and causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Request rate flat (F9) with no surge; CPU ~36% and memory ~57% flat (F10); pool_pool_in_use pinned exactly at the new cap of 5 (F6), indicating an artificial limit, not organic overload.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db (shared Postgres) slow/IOPS-throttled causing portfolio-service DB waits
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db degraded, slowing queries and causing portfolio-service connection waits.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Errors are explicit pool-acquire timeouts at exactly the new pool limit of 5 (F4, F6), not query/statement timeouts; ledger-db latency could not be measured (F14) but pool sizing math fully explains the symptom. order/payment also use ledger-db and are unaffected.

facts.statement: Onset of api-gateway latency/error degradation is the 09:45-09:48 buckets, immediately after the 09:52 config change and 09:53 first portfolio error.
portfolio-service Hikari pool is capped at exactly 5 connections with zero idle and many waiters, matching db.pool.max_size=new_value 5.
Gateways errors are downstream propagation of portfolio-service timeouts on /v1/portfolio/holdings (504).
No load/CPU/memory anomaly accompanied the incident.
The suspected gateway h2 deploy (08:00) is timely implausible and its sibling upstream order-service is unaffected.

assumptions: cfg-2207 was the only change affecting the portfolio-service datasource in this window.
Normal traffic (~560 req/s) genuinely required more than 5 DB connections.
Absence of earlier errors reflects healthy behavior, not missing telemetry.

timeline.event: dep-5220 api-gateway v9.3.0 deployed (envoy 1.30, HTTP/2 to portfolio-service and order-service)
portfolio-service p99 rises to 2556ms avg (bucket); gateway p99 2148ms and 5xx 3.75%
portfolio-service first ERROR: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms; Hikari total=5 idle=0 waiting rising
api-gateway first 504 upstream timeout to portfolio-service /v1/portfolio/holdings
Steady state: gateway p99 ~4.3s / 7.2% 5xx; portfolio p99 ~4.15s; db_pool_in_use pinned at 5.0
Pool exhaustion still ongoing at end of data (total=5)

recommended_actions.action: Revert cfg-2207 immediately: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size to 50 (or an empirically sized value).
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool cap of 5 is the direct cause of the JDBC acquire timeouts; restoring it removes the bottleneck.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery by watching portfolio-service Hikari idle>0 / db_pool_in_use and gateway p99 returning to ~200ms after the revert.
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the causal chain and that no second fault exists.

recommended_actions.action: Add validation/guards so automated cost-optimisation profiles cannot reduce datasource pool size below a service-safe minimum, and require review for prod datasource changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 was applied by infra-automation; HIST-115 was the same class of pool misconfiguration.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back dep-5220 as the primary mitigation; if desired, validate h2 upgrade separately (order-service already unaffected).
recommended_actions.rationale: Timing and sibling-service evidence exonerate the gateway deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument Hikari pool saturation (idle, waiting, acquire-timeout rate) with alerting so pool exhaustion pages before user-visible 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: Exhaustion ran from 09:53 to 11:58 without an automated page.

data_gaps: ledger-db latency/health could not be retrieved (query timed out 3x) — cannot fully rule out slow-query contributions, though the evidence points to pool sizing.
No direct datapoint for portfolio-service request concurrency/queue depth beyond db_pool_in_use and Hikari 'waiting' counts.
No explicit confirmation that cfg-2207 was the sole datasource-affecting change on portfolio-service (assumed).

findings.statement: api-gateway p99 latency rose from ~205-215ms (steady 06:00-09:30) to 2148ms avg at the 09:45 bucket and ~4300ms from 10:00 onward; max 4711.85ms.
api-gateway error_rate (5xx) rose from ~0.2% to 3.75% in the 09:48 bucket and settled at ~7.2% from 10:00 onward.
portfolio-service p99 latency rose from ~180ms to 2555.91ms avg in the 09:48 bucket and ~4150ms from 10:00 (max 4575.38ms).
portfolio-service began logging ERROR 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' at 09:53:19, and HikariPool reports exhaustion with 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43'.

findings.statement: A config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service set db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z (author infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource').
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was ~12 connections before the change, then dropped to and pinned at exactly 5.0 for the whole period after 10:00.

The only code deployment in the window is dep-5220 on api-gateway (v9.3.0) at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' for portfolio-service and order-service; it is still live with no rollback.
order-service, the other upstream that dep-5220 switched to HTTP/2, shows no latency change: p99 flat ~148-153ms across the whole 08:00-11:59 window.
portfolio-service request_rate was flat at ~560-580 req/s across the incident, with no surge at onset.
portfolio-service cpu_pct stayed flat at ~35-36% and memory_pct at ~57% throughout, showing no resource exhaustion.
api-gateway logs during the incident are dominated by 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504', confirming the gateway symptom is downstream of portfolio-service.
The pool exhaustion persisted continuously from 09:53 through the end of data at 11:58, still reporting total=5.

findings.statement: Historical incident HIST-115 (order-service, 2025-09-25) had the same symptom class — 'connection is not available / pool exhausted' — with root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change.
